page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-80 is an x86_64 cloud server featuring 80 virtual CPUs and 40 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. With two threads per core and dedicated CPU allocation, the instance includes 640 GB of total system RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is none, and the instance operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs. CPU cache architecture provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction support for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and ADX.

Benchmark outcomes show high performance across parallelized compute and memory-centric operations. In multi-threaded evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier cryptographic performance, attaining 85,542.27 on the PassMark CPU encryption test alongside a multi-core stress-ng metric of 108,034.75 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,162.0. Memory subsystem testing reflects strong cached bandwidth at 4,733.91 GB/sec for small 16 KB read blocks, supporting elevated throughput in database operations with a PassMark database score of 25,094.59 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 67.8 million operations per second.

Tradeoffs manifest primarily in single-threaded processing and massive-model machine learning operations. Geekbench single-core execution registers at 1,522.0, placing single-threaded throughput in an average tier. Furthermore, while lightweight LLM inference runs capably on CPU threads, large 70B parameter models reach only 2.4 tokens per second during text generation due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. Large-block memory transfers also level off at average ratings, including 123.55 GB/sec for read and 63.07 GB/sec for write operations.

The 1:8 core-to-memory configuration delivers high resource density for enterprise workloads requiring extensive RAM allocations without dedicating hardware to GPU compute. This makes the n2d-highmem-80 well suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, and multi-threaded analytical data processing.
